item.title: In Canada: Drake Breaks Records for Most No. 1s Ever on the Billboard Canadian Hot 100 & Album Charts
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest music news and trends. Today, we're talking about a record-breaking artist and some exciting updates from the Canadian music scene.
First up, Drake is making waves on the Billboard Canadian charts. His latest release, "Iceman", has broken multiple records, including the most No. 1 songs on the Canadian Hot 100 chart. With 14 chart-topping songs, Drake has surpassed Justin Bieber and Taylor Swift, taking the top spot for himself.
[Short music clip]
Host: But that's not all - Drake is dominating the Canadian Hot 100 chart, occupying 9 out of the top 10 spots simultaneously. He's also broken Taylor Swift's record for the most entries in the top 20, with 17 songs charting at the same time.
[Short music clip]
Host: In other news, the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission, or CRTC, has made some significant updates to its regulations for online streaming platforms. Major streaming services like Netflix and Amazon Prime Video will now be required to pay 15% of their income to Canadian content funds, a 10% increase from the previous proposal.
[Short music clip]
Host: This move aims to boost Canadian and Indigenous content discoverability, ensuring that Canadian stories continue to be told and made available to audiences across the country.
[Outro music plays]
Host: And that's a wrap for today's episode. We'll be keeping an eye on these developments and bringing you more updates soon. Thanks for tuning in, and we'll catch you in the next one!
